purpose: Audit trail for every file removed during the phase 4/5 consolidation. The integration plan's biggest execution risk is deleting code that looked dead and was not. This log makes each deletion auditable, and tests/contract/test_deletion_log.py makes the log itself enforced: an entry without a reason or a verification fails the build, and a deleted path that reappears fails it too.
policy: A path may only be deleted after its importers have been checked with a whole-repository search, not a guess.
Verification records what was actually run, so a reviewer can repeat it rather than trust it.
Anything not listed here is not an approved deletion. If it vanishes, that is a finding.
A deletion that turns out to have been live is restored with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`; every entry in this log is a tracked file, so no deletion here is irreversible.

excluded.git submodules: lib/forge-std and lib/openzeppelin-contracts are gitmodules. Their directories are populated; only the index entry differs. They are not part of this log and must not be touched by consolidation work.

name_collision_with_live_package.note: The deleted file was a module named engine.hydroma.core, and a package of the same name sits beside it. Python always resolves the package, so no import statement can distinguish them and every  rom engine.hydroma.core import X in the tree is satisfied by the package. Tests that grep for the file by name must not be read as live importers.

restore_audit.finding: The documented undo command `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` does not work for these entries. They were deleted before the deletion was committed, so the files were never present in HEAD. The standard requires a logged deletion to be recoverable; these are not.
restore_audit.cause: commit faeda9d9 ('one-shot final cleanup') added and removed these paths in the same commit, so no ancestor tree contains them either.
restore_audit.action_taken: none - no source tree may reconstruct them
restore_audit.note: Recording this is not cosmetic. Until it is resolved, the deletion log overstates recoverability, and test_deletion_safety.py correctly fails.

supersession_audit.finding: engine/resilience.py is named as the replacement for the deleted services/api_gateway/resilience/ package, but it has zero importers. The supersession was declared, not performed: nothing in services/ or the eventbus calls get_circuit_breaker or circuit_breaker.
supersession_audit.consequence: Outbound calls have no circuit breaker. Retry and timeout behaviour comes only from the HTTP client libraries, so the resilience layer the log implies exists does not run.
supersession_audit.reason: Azure Architecture Center lists a circuit breaker as NOT suitable when the dependency already retries, and Google SRE ch.22 warns that layered retries multiply load. The correct next step is an inventory of which outbound calls actually need one, not wiring it everywhere.
supersession_audit.verified_by: grep for get_circuit_breaker / circuit_breaker across services/ and engine/ consumers: 0 matches
